Most standard set implementations (e.g., `HashSet`, `TreeSet` with natural ordering for `String`) accept `String` objects without issue. Therefore, this exception is avoided by the type compatibility of the arguments.
- `NullPointerException`: The `name` parameter is used directly without a null check. If a caller passes `null` for `name`, and `failedSymbols` does not permit null elements (e.g., `TreeSet`, `LinkedHashSet` with no null support), then the call will throw `NullPointerException`. The code does not guard against `name` being null (e.g., no if-null check or try-catch). Therefore, this exception is NOT avoided.
